summary: Dienes & Perner cold-control theory: hypnosis = executive control WITHOUT higher-order thoughts (HOTs) about intending; explains involuntariness (the 'classical suggestion effect'). Bridges state and social-psychological accounts; compatible with Hilgard neodissociation under 'no HOTs' reading.
content: Dienes & Perner 'cold control theory of hypnosis' (chapter): hypnosis = forming an intention to perform the suggested action WITHOUT forming the higher-order thoughts (HOTs) about intending that action. Explains the 'classical suggestion effect' (Weitzenhoffer 1974) — the experience of involuntariness. Explicitly notes the theory BRIDGES traditions: 'cold control can also be simply described at the personal level... entirely consistent with the social psychological approach... Where cold control theory goes beyond social psychological approaches is in a specific commitment to HOT theory.' Compatible with Hilgard neodissociation under the 'no HOTs' interpretation. Makes testable brain-imaging predictions distinguishing cold control from 'empty heat.'
